solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soon comes round to dump rubbish — something tiny discovered

indicators.note: the word for soon wraps around the other pieces, so it sits on the outside

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
a tip is a rubbish dump
rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone will shortly go to the tip to get rid of junk, and finds something tiny there.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle, the antimatter twin of a proton, was discovered in 1955: a tiny thing found by physicists.

clue.text: A horse is a poor performer when lacking part of harness

indicators.note: lacking says a piece is taken away from the word before

parts.note: a rabbit is a weak player, especially a tail-end batsman in cricket
the bit is the mouthpiece of a horse's harness

explanation.surface: A horse is useless if part of its tack is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: A rabbit is British slang for a poor player at a sport such as cricket or tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arab is a well-known breed of horse from the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: What's not right is concealed by party politics

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the two words that follow, straddling them

explanation.surface: Something wrong is being covered up through political party manoeuvring.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'parTY POlitics'.
explanation.definitionFit: A misprint is a small error, something on the page that is not correct.

clue.text: Sharp lawyers decked out in special gear for supplicants

indicators.note: decked out means dressed up, so the letters are rearranged into a new outfit

explanation.surface: Smart lawyers are dressed in distinctive clothing for people who come begging.
explanation.definitionFit: Jewish worshippers wear a tallit, a fringed garment, when praying, so it is clothing for people at prayer.

clue.text: Nervous, looking down at Much Wenlock?

definitions.meaning: Much Wenlock is a Shropshire town beneath Wenlock Edge, a long wooded ridge, so someone up there looks down on it

explanation.surface: Someone anxious peers down at a small English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Much Wenlock is a small town in Shropshire, England, overlooked by the escarpment called Wenlock Edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Jittery and tense is the idiomatic sense; the second reading places a person standing on Wenlock Edge.

clue.text: I drink in exam, being odd in character

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the word for an exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone having a drink during a test is behaving strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric or unconventional person is called a true one-off, distinctively odd in their character.

clue.text: Negotiators employed by Barclays regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the bank's name

explanation.surface: A bank uses people to negotiate on its behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of bArClAyS. ACAS is Britain's Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, which mediates in workplace disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: This UK public body brokers settlements between employers and unions, so its staff are mediators in disputes.

clue.text: Good content in TV soap and bad things to be put right

indicators.note: content means contained, so the letter goes inside the soap's name

parts.note: Corrie is the nickname of Coronation Street, a long-running British TV soap opera

indicators.note: bad signals the word and is rearranged

explanation.surface: A soap opera holds something wholesome and also bad things needing correction.
explanation.walkthrough: Coronation Street is a long-running British TV soap, nicknamed Corrie.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of errors in a book that need correcting is printed under this Latin plural heading.

clue.text: African to experience biting winds in Durham?

indicators.note: biting means holding between the teeth, so the outer word clamps around the rest

parts.note: to see something is to experience it
Durham is in the North East of England, NE, so winds there are NE gales

explanation.surface: Someone from Africa feels the cold, biting winds of County Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biting' puts NE GALES inside SEE. Durham is a county in North East England.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Senegal, a country in West Africa, is an African by nationality.

clue.text: As a host is showing certain things in their natural order?

definitions.text: As a host is showing certain things in their natural order?

parts.words: As a host is showing certain things in their natural order
parts.note: the letters of 'host' run H, O, S, T, as do those of 'As', each in dictionary order, so the word shows letters in their natural sequence

explanation.surface: A party host displays some items in their proper order.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'certain things' are letters: in the words 'As' and 'host' they already stand in A-to-Z order.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged in A-to-Z sequence describes letters sorted as the alphabet runs.

clue.text: A third of fruit going off in African port

indicators.note: going off means leaving, so a part of the fruit's name is removed

parts.note: an orange is a fruit
a third of a six-letter word is two letters, here the last two

explanation.surface: Some fruit goes bad in a port in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' removes GE, a third of ORANGE's six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oran is a major Mediterranean port city in Algeria, North Africa.

clue.text: End up as many will when visiting a cathedral

definitions.text: as many will when visiting a cathedral
definitions.meaning: a cathedral close is the enclosed precinct round a cathedral, which visitors approach

explanation.surface: Tourists reach a cathedral, where their trip ends.
explanation.walkthrough: A close is the walled grounds around a British cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish is the idiom; literally, visitors arrive at the precinct surrounding a cathedral.

clue.text: I go expanding out as Communist statesman

indicators.note: out means not in place, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A politician declares that he is getting bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Chinese Communist leader who opened China's economy to the world from 1978.

clue.text: 'Quire' (unusual spelling!) having energy in pleasant piece of music

indicators.note: in places the rearranged word and the letter inside the word for pleasant

parts.note: warm weather is pleasant

indicators.note: an unusual spelling of a word jumbles its letters

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An odd spelling of a choir word appears in a charming work of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual spelling' looks like a comment on the quoted word, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten's 1962 choral work setting the Latin Mass for the dead with Wilfred Owen's poems.

clue.text: Bits of good pie now put out for wild bird

indicators.note: bits of means the words broken into pieces
put out means disturbed, so the pieces are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: Scraps of tasty pie are left outside to feed a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This large grey pigeon lives wild in British woods and fields, a common bird.

clue.text: Set off to celebrate wildly with leader deposed

indicators.note: deposed means removed, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to carouse is to drink and celebrate noisily

explanation.surface: A wild party begins after the boss is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with leader deposed' drops the C from CAROUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger or stir up a feeling is to provoke it into action, as in setting off anger.

clue.text: One to blossom as dissenter imprisoned by bullying prince

indicators.note: the second word is shut inside the first like a captive

parts.note: Prince Hal, the future Henry V; in Shakespeare's Henry V, Pistol calls the king 'the lovely bully'
a rebel dissents from authority

explanation.surface: A rebel locked up by a domineering prince will flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V; 'bullying' nods to Pistol calling him 'the lovely bully'.
explanation.definitionFit: This blue bell-shaped wild flower is a plant that blooms, so something that will flower.

clue.text: A resident shortly to be off is left in Britain

indicators.note: off means wrong, so the letters are rearranged
shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

explanation.surface: A local resident is about to depart from Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims A RESIDENT to A RESIDEN, and 'to be off' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: British cars drive on the left, so the kerb side of a vehicle there is its left.

clue.text: Disconcerted as one revealing planted kiss?

definitions.meaning: a cheek marked with lipstick shows where a kiss was planted

explanation.surface: Someone is embarrassed because a lipstick mark gives away a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Blushing with embarrassment is the idiom; literally a cheek stained by lipstick.

clue.text: Apartments in which criminals will hold party

indicators.note: hold means contain, so the outer word surrounds the inner

parts.note: cons are convicts, criminals
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Crooks throw a party in some flats.
explanation.definitionFit: In North American usage these are individually owned flats in a block.

clue.text: One African country thus introduces another one's language

indicators.note: introduces means comes in front of, so this piece goes first

parts.note: so means thus
Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: An African country passes its language on to a neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'another (African country)'s language', the tongue of Somalia.
explanation.definitionFit: The official language of Somalia, in the Horn of Africa, a different country from Mali.

clue.text: Author with pen swivelling about on seat

indicators.note: on means following, so the seat comes next

parts.note: a quill is a pen made from a feather

indicators.note: swivelling means turning round, so the short word is read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a couch is a seat

explanation.surface: A writer turns round with his pen, sitting on a sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swivelling' turns RE into ER. Sir Arthur Quiller-Couch, 'Q', was a Cornish novelist and editor of the Oxford Book of English Verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Quiller-Couch was a writer, novelist and literary critic, so a man of letters.

clue.text: A sharp change of direction going up a troubled region

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a zag is a sharp turn, as in zigzag

explanation.surface: A sudden swerve heads up into a war-torn area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns ZAG into GAZ.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaza Strip on the Mediterranean is a long-contested area in the Middle East conflict.

clue.text: Stone horse not in prime condition

definitions.meaning: a green gemstone used for carving

explanation.surface: A rock and a tired old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a green ornamental gem and a broken-down nag go by this word.

clue.text: Composer offers no introductory key

indicators.note: no introductory means the opening letter is not there

parts.note: gives means offers
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A musician offers no opening key for his piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no introductory' removes G from GIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American modernist who wrote symphonies and songs.

clue.text: A small drink knocked back by boy in company, a rum-based potation

indicators.note: knocked back means turned back, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a nip is a small measure of spirits
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy at a party downs a small drink and then a rum cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reads A NIP backwards as PINA; 'knocked back' looks like drinking it down.
explanation.definitionFit: This cocktail is made with rum, coconut cream and pineapple juice, a drink based on rum.

clue.text: Religious troublemaker you turned away

indicators.note: away means taken off, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a monkey is a mischievous child

indicators.note: turned means reversed, so the old word for you is read backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A troublemaker in a religious order is sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses YE to EY, and 'away' removes it from MONKEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords use 'religious' as a noun for a member of a religious order, such as a friar.

clue.text: Paper boss rejected free debate

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper
to liberate is to free

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor refuses to allow an open discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ED into DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to discuss carefully and weigh up, a verb sense of debate.
